title: W07b: worker call forwarding through the native MCP client
description: Forward every supported worker call through Hermes's existing MCP client, with no private parallel client and no general shell proxy: obtain host-provided session, worker and profile context; resolve and validate exactly one binding; validate registration, pinned route, worktree, binding generation and required ownership context; resolve the operation from the generated allowlisted catalog; supply the bound actor and worker context and reject attempts to override them; forward to the project-bound server; decode transport and Waystation results separately while preserving both diagnostics; and release in-flight accounting without changing the binding. Validate the inner result rather than trusting transport success, never automatically replay a claim, message or handoff mutation on a lost response, and report an unknown outcome when a truncated response may follow a completed write. Read responses stay inside the payload budget with pagination or chunking, canonical message bodies are never truncated to fit a wrapper, and the adapter validates result shape and types rather than looking for prose such as success.
acceptance: Outer transport success with an inner failure is reported as failure, and a malformed or truncated response is reported as an unknown outcome for writes rather than as success or as nothing having happened.
Model-supplied actor or context overrides are rejected, and a call with a missing or ambiguous binding never falls back to a startup working directory or a default profile route.
Read payloads stay inside the budget with pagination in place, and a canonical message body is never truncated to fit a wrapper.
A disabled plugin, an absent MCP allowlist entry, an unavailable server and a missing grant each produce a distinct refusal instead of a degraded fallback.
notes: Acceptance group A13. Each project is one MCP server entry with the ledger encoded in its command arguments, so per-project isolation comes from the server name and explicit arguments, never from the caller's working directory.
